registry_snapshot.name: IS_PLAN
registry_snapshot.definition: The reasoning explicitly expresses at least one intended future action or a sequence of intended future actions that the agent commits to performing.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text expressing the intended future action or sequence of actions.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning explicitly identifies at least one intended future action.
The intended action is presented as something the agent will do next, rather than as a mere possibility or a restatement of the task.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning only reports actions already completed.
The reasoning only restates task requirements without committing to a future action.

registry_snapshot.name: SPECIFIES_CORRECTIVE_CONTENT_WITH_JUSTIFICATION
registry_snapshot.definition: The reasoning supplies concrete content intended to correct, complete, or otherwise modify an artifact and justifies why that content satisfies the target requirement, optionally by evaluating and rejecting an alternative that would fail.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text that states the concrete replacement or completion content and the justification for its correctness.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning states concrete content to be applied to the artifact, such as specific steps, replacement text, or a proof script, not merely the intention to change it.
The reasoning explains why the stated content achieves the goal, using the semantics of the relevant domain entities.
If alternative candidates are considered, at least one is rejected for an identified reason.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning only describes the defect or goal without supplying concrete content to apply.
The reasoning only lists generic strategies without indicating which one will be used or why it works.

registry_snapshot.name: GROUNDS_CONCLUSION_IN_OBSERVATION
registry_snapshot.definition: The reasoning draws a conclusion using identifiable content of the observation as supporting evidence for that conclusion.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The reasoning expressing the evidence-based conclusion.

parameters.name: observation
parameters.description: The observation supplying the evidence used for that conclusion.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning states a conclusion that goes beyond restating the observation, such as a judgment about correctness, availability, or completion.
Identifiable content of the observation, such as values, listed artifacts, returned text, or computed output, is used as support for that conclusion.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning merely repeats or summarizes the observation without drawing a conclusion from it.
The observation is unrelated to the conclusion or contains nothing that supports it.

registry_snapshot.name: DIAGNOSES_FAILURE_AND_PRESCRIBES_CORRECTION
registry_snapshot.definition: An observation reports a failed outcome; the reasoning identifies a specific cause for the failure that links it to the semantics of the executed operation, and prescribes a corrective action that differs from the failed one in the diagnosed respect.

parameters.name: failure_observation
parameters.description: The observation reporting the error or unsuccessful outcome.

parameters.name: diagnosis_reasoning
parameters.description: The reasoning explaining the cause of the failure and specifying the corrected approach.

parameters.name: corrective_action
parameters.description: The action that applies the corrected approach prescribed by the diagnosis.

assertion_conditions: The observation reports an error or otherwise unsuccessful result.
The reasoning states a specific cause for the failure rather than merely noting that it failed.
The reasoning specifies how the operation must be changed in light of that cause.
The corrective action implements that change and is therefore distinguishable from the failed action.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning retries the same operation without identifying a cause or changing the approach.
The reasoning speculates about causes unrelated to the reported error.
The corrective action does not reflect the stated diagnosis.

registry_snapshot.name: TESTS_ASSUMPTION_WITH_PROBE
registry_snapshot.definition: A targeted action queries the environment to resolve a specific uncertainty or unverified prerequisite identified in reasoning, and the resulting observation provides evidence that settles or materially informs it before dependent work proceeds.

parameters.name: assumption_reasoning
parameters.description: The reasoning identifying the uncertainty or prerequisite that must be settled.

parameters.name: probe_action
parameters.description: The action performing the targeted query about that uncertainty.

parameters.name: probe_result
parameters.description: The observation reporting the result relevant to the uncertainty.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning identifies a specific open question or prerequisite condition whose value is not yet known.
The probe action is directed at obtaining exactly that information from the environment.
The observation returns information that resolves or materially informs the identified question.
exclusion_conditions: No identifiable uncertainty or prerequisite motivates the action.
The action is unrelated to the stated question, or the observation does not address it.
The probe merely repeats information already established earlier in the trajectory.

registry_snapshot.name: VERIFIES_REQUIREMENT_SATISFACTION
registry_snapshot.definition: After an outcome has been produced, a separate verification action inspects the produced artifact or result, its observation demonstrates the required property directly rather than only the absence of errors, and the reasoning concludes from it that the requirement is satisfied.

parameters.name: verification_action
parameters.description: The action that inspects or exercises the already produced outcome.

parameters.name: verification_observation
parameters.description: The observation containing content that demonstrates the required property.

parameters.name: concluding_reasoning
parameters.description: The reasoning concluding that the requirement is met on the basis of that observation.

assertion_conditions: The verification action is distinct from the action that produced the outcome and targets the produced artifact or result.
The observation exposes content showing the required property actually holds, for example the resulting object is present and carries the expected content.
The reasoning explicitly concludes that the requirement is satisfied, citing that observation.
exclusion_conditions: The action is the one that produced the outcome rather than an independent check of it.
The observation only indicates that no error occurred, without demonstrating the required property.
No conclusion is drawn from the observation, or the conclusion is not tied to it.

registry_snapshot.name: ENUMERATES_REQUIRED_COMPONENTS
registry_snapshot.definition: The reasoning decomposes a stated goal into multiple distinct components, accounts, permissions, or artifacts that must exist for the goal to be satisfiable, turning the goal description into identifiable configuration obligations.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text listing the components or artifacts that must exist for the stated goal to be satisfiable.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning identifies multiple distinct elements that must exist or be configured, such as an account, a repository, a deployment mechanism, or a serving process.
Each identified element is justified by the goal's expected usage or by an explicit dependency of the goal rather than being listed arbitrarily.
The enumeration includes required state, artifacts, or configuration obligations beyond merely ordering actions to perform.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning only restates the goal without identifying required elements.
The reasoning only gives an ordered procedure or action plan without identifying what must exist.
The reasoning proposes only a single required element or an incidental detail.

registry_snapshot.name: IMPLEMENTS_PLANNED_STEP
registry_snapshot.definition: The action carries out a concrete operation or creates/configures an artifact that the reasoning explicitly identified as an intended step, so the action is the observable execution of a previously stated intention.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The recorded tool invocation that performs the intended step.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The reasoning that explicitly states the intended step which the action executes.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning explicitly names the operation or artifact that the action then operates on before that action occurs.
The action's content matches the intended step in purpose and target, not merely in topic.
The action executes that intended step rather than an unrelated exploration.
exclusion_conditions: The action explores the environment without a corresponding previously stated intention.
The reasoning mentions the operation or artifact only after the action's result is known.
The action's target or purpose differs from the stated intention.

registry_snapshot.name: ANTICIPATES_PROCEDURAL_PITFALL
registry_snapshot.definition: The reasoning predicts a specific failure mode or unusable outcome that would arise from a default or naive procedure and states a preventive or corrective configuration measure derived from that prediction.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text that predicts the failure mode and states the preventive or corrective measure.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning describes a concrete way the default or planned procedure could fail or produce an unusable result.
The reasoning links that predicted failure to a preventive or corrective measure that changes the procedure or configuration.
The predicted failure is prospective rather than an already observed error.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning observes a failure that has already occurred rather than predicting one.
The reasoning lists general best practices without linking them to an identified failure mode.
The reasoning predicts a failure but does not state any measure addressing it.

registry_snapshot.name: VALIDATES_BEFORE_ACTIVATION
registry_snapshot.definition: An action applies a configuration to a service or running system only after an explicit validity check of that configuration within the same invocation, and the observation reports both the successful validation and the activated or applied service.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The tool invocation that performs the configuration validity check and then applies or activates the configuration.

parameters.name: observation
parameters.description: The tool result reporting the validation outcome and the activation or application state of the service.

assertion_conditions: The action includes an explicit validation of the configuration before starting, reloading, or otherwise applying it.
Activation or application is conditioned on that validation succeeding within the same invocation.
The observation reports the validation as successful and shows the service running or the configuration applied.
exclusion_conditions: The service is started without any preceding configuration validation.
Validation is performed but activation or application does not follow.
The observation shows a validation failure or no evidence that the service is active or the configuration applied.
Validation and activation occur in separate invocations, or the validation concerns an unrelated configuration.

registry_snapshot.name: SIMULATES_END_USER_WORKFLOW
registry_snapshot.definition: The action reproduces the operation sequence that an external consumer (the requester or a client) would perform against the assembled system, using throwaway credentials or scratch artifacts, in order to validate the system as it will be experienced by that consumer rather than to produce the final deliverable configuration.

parameters.name: simulating_action
parameters.description: The tool invocation that executes the reproduced consumer-side operation sequence.

parameters.name: consumer_perspective_reasoning
parameters.description: Reasoning that frames the upcoming operation as acting like the requester or external client and explains that the sequence is a simulation for validation.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning frames the upcoming operation as what the requester or an external client would do against the system.
The action performs a multi-step sequence matching that consumer behavior, distinct from the configuration or installation steps that constitute the deliverable.
The action relies on throwaway artifacts such as temporary credentials or scratch locations, so the simulation does not itself become part of the final state.
The stated purpose is to exercise the system as a consumer would, not to build the deliverable.
exclusion_conditions: The action is an ordinary configuration or installation step that constitutes the deliverable itself.
The action is a single isolated probe of one component rather than the consumer-visible operation sequence.
The reasoning does not connect the action to consumer-side behavior.
The action is not executed with throwaway artifacts and therefore permanently alters the delivered state.

registry_snapshot.name: OBSERVATION_CONFIRMS_EXPECTED_OUTCOME
registry_snapshot.definition: The observation reports exactly the result that the reasoning had predicted or required before the result was obtained, so the previously stated expectation can be judged satisfied rather than merely error-free.

parameters.name: expectation_reasoning
parameters.description: Reasoning stating the concrete expected or required outcome before the result is inspected.

parameters.name: confirming_observation
parameters.description: The tool result whose content corresponds to that expected outcome.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning states a concrete expected outcome (a value, response, or state) before the corresponding observation is available.
The observation contains content corresponding to that expectation, allowing the expectation to be judged satisfied rather than merely free of errors.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning states no expected outcome, so the result cannot be judged against an expectation.
The observation reports a different or partial result than the one expected.
The observation is unrelated to the expectation expressed in the reasoning.
The expectation is formulated only after the result has already been observed.

registry_snapshot.name: RECOGNIZES_INCONCLUSIVE_TOOL_RESULT
registry_snapshot.definition: The reasoning determines that an observation, although not reported as an error, fails to answer the question it was meant to answer because of a limitation of the method or tool used, and specifies a different method intended to obtain the missing information.

parameters.name: reassessment_reasoning
parameters.description: Reasoning that identifies the inadequacy of the earlier result, attributes it to a method limitation, and specifies an alternative method.

parameters.name: uninformative_observation
parameters.description: The observation whose output is empty, truncated, or otherwise uninformative for the intended question without being flagged as an error.

assertion_conditions: The observation returned output that does not answer the intended question, and the observation is not flagged as an error.
The reasoning attributes the missing information to a limitation of the command, tool, or method form used.
The reasoning specifies a different command, option, or method intended to produce the missing information.
exclusion_conditions: The observation answers the question adequately, so no replacement method is needed.
The observation reports an explicit failure that is diagnosed as a defect cause rather than a method limitation.
The reasoning retries the identical method without changing it.
The reasoning only notes that the output is empty without attributing it to a method limitation or proposing an alternative.

registry_snapshot.name: RESTORES_PRISTINE_STATE_AFTER_TEST
registry_snapshot.definition: Following verification or test activity, the agent deliberately removes or resets the artifacts created by that activity so the system returns to the state a later consumer expects to encounter before any such activity occurred.

parameters.name: cleanup_reasoning
parameters.description: Reasoning that enumerates the artifacts created during verification and states the target initial state to restore.

parameters.name: cleanup_actions
parameters.description: The actions that delete, reset, or purge those artifacts; collectively they restore the pre-test state.

parameters.name: state_observation
parameters.description: The observation showing the post-cleanup state of the affected resources.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning identifies artifacts created by the agent's own verification or test activity and states that they must be removed or reset to an initial state.
The cleanup actions delete, reset, or empty those identified artifacts.
The state observation shows the affected resources emptied or matching the intended initial configuration.
exclusion_conditions: No artifacts were created by the agent's own verification activity, so there is nothing to restore.
The cleanup leaves the identified artifacts in place, or the observation shows them still present because the removal failed.
The deletion is part of ordinary construction rather than restoring a state that a later consumer should encounter.

registry_snapshot.name: VERIFIES_RUNTIME_SERVICE_STATE
registry_snapshot.definition: An inspection action queries the actual runtime state of deployed services, such as running processes, listening sockets, or an exercised endpoint, and the observation shows the intended services active at the intended endpoints.

parameters.name: inspection_action
parameters.description: The tool invocation that queries the running state of the deployed services.

parameters.name: runtime_observation
parameters.description: The tool result listing processes, listening addresses, or endpoint responses that reveal the services' actual runtime state.

assertion_conditions: The action queries the actual running state of the services (processes, sockets, or an exercised endpoint) rather than only the content of their configuration files.
The observation reports the intended services present and active, with the expected endpoints or listening addresses visible.
exclusion_conditions: The action modifies configuration or starts services instead of inspecting runtime state.
The observation only shows configuration syntax validity without any evidence of running state.
The observation shows the service absent or not listening on the intended endpoint.
The observation concerns a resource unrelated to the deployed services.

registry_snapshot.name: ADDS_AVAILABILITY_SAFEGUARD
registry_snapshot.definition: The agent installs a recovery mechanism that restores a component's availability when it is later found stopped, motivated by anticipated future interruptions or restarts rather than by the needs of the immediate request.

parameters.name: safeguard_reasoning
parameters.description: Reasoning that motivates the extra recovery mechanism as protection against future interruptions or restarts.

parameters.name: safeguard_action
parameters.description: The tool invocation that creates or installs the recovery mechanism.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning frames the addition as protection against a future interruption, restart, or unavailability rather than as a step needed for the current request to work.
The action creates or installs a mechanism that checks whether the component is present and restarts or restores it when absent.
The mechanism is designed to be safe to invoke repeatedly, so it can act as an automatic safeguard.
exclusion_conditions: The action is ordinary service startup required for the current request to work at all.
The mechanism cannot restore a stopped component or would fail the calling shell on error.
No reasoning connects the mechanism to future availability concerns.
The installed mechanism only reports status without restoring the component.

accepted_predicates.name: DECLARES_TASK_COMPLETE
accepted_predicates.definition: The reasoning asserts that the overall goal of the task has been achieved and supports that claim by summarizing or enumerating the delivered components, configuration, or verified outcomes, rather than reporting only that one isolated step succeeded.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text concluding that the overall task is finished and summarizing or enumerating what was delivered or verified.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning explicitly asserts that the overall task or goal is complete.
The completion claim is accompanied by a summary or enumeration of the delivered components, configuration state, or verified outcomes.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning reports only an intermediate step's success without claiming overall completion.
The reasoning expresses an intention to finish later rather than asserting that the task is finished.

accepted_predicates.name: EXPLAINS_ANOMALOUS_OBSERVATION
accepted_predicates.definition: The reasoning treats a recorded observation as anomalous — empty, absent, unexpected, or inconsistent with the check that produced it — and attributes the anomaly to a specific identifiable mechanism, so the anomalous content is not taken at face value as evidence about the condition the check was designed to reveal.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text that flags the result as unexpected, empty, or absent and proposes a specific explanation for it.

parameters.name: observation
parameters.description: The observation whose output is empty, missing, unexpected, or otherwise inconsistent with the intent of the action that produced it.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning explicitly notes that the observation's result is empty, missing, unexpected, or otherwise not what the check was designed to reveal.
The reasoning attributes the anomaly to an identifiable mechanism, such as a limitation of the command or tool form, an unfollowed link, or an artifact of how the process was launched.
The reasoning thereby reinterprets the anomalous result so that it is not automatically treated as evidence against the condition under investigation.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning reads the observation at face value as evidence about the condition it was meant to check.
The reasoning reports the unexpected or empty result without offering any causal explanation.
The reasoning attributes the result only to a generic failure without identifying a mechanism.

accepted_predicates.name: AUDITS_STATE_AGAINST_ENUMERATED_CRITERIA
accepted_predicates.definition: The reasoning enumerates multiple independent conditions that must hold for success, a single action collects evidence for those conditions in one combined inspection, and the observation reports state values that can be matched against the enumerated conditions.

parameters.name: criteria_reasoning
parameters.description: The reasoning enumerating the multiple independent conditions or state facts to be audited.

parameters.name: audit_action
parameters.description: The action that gathers state evidence for the enumerated conditions in one combined inspection.

parameters.name: audit_result
parameters.description: The observation reporting state values or findings that correspond to the enumerated conditions, including any gaps.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning explicitly enumerates two or more distinct conditions or state facts that must hold for success.
The action collects evidence for those conditions within a single combined inspection rather than one check per condition.
The observation reports values or findings that can be matched one-to-one against the enumerated conditions.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning checks only a single condition.
The observation does not report on the enumerated conditions, so the result cannot be matched against them.
No criteria are stated before the inspection, so the result cannot be judged against them.

accepted_predicates.name: INSPECTS_STATE_WITHOUT_MODIFICATION
accepted_predicates.definition: The action only reads or queries pre-existing system state — processes, sockets, files, references, permissions, or an exercised endpoint — and does not itself create, modify, or delete persistent configuration, file content, or data.

parameters.name: inspection_action
parameters.description: The action that reads or queries existing state for evidence gathering.

assertion_conditions: The action's arguments consist of read-only queries against state that already exists in the environment.
No persistent configuration, file content, or data is created, modified, or deleted by the action.
The purpose of the action is to obtain information about the environment rather than to change it.
exclusion_conditions: The action writes, appends, deletes, or otherwise changes persistent state.
The action both inspects and mutates state within the same invocation, so persistent state differs after it runs.
